children: The combination of resilient economic growth and a gradual rise in inflation could give Bank Negara Malaysia room to increase its policy rate to 3.0%, OCBC economist Lavanya Venkateswaran says in a note. Those factors would reduce the need to maintain a slightly accommodative monetary-policy stance, she says. Although BNM's concluding remarks were little changed from the previous meeting, she reiterates her expectation of a rate increase to 3.00% at January's meeting. The main risk is that the central bank may take longer to assess the need to normalize rates, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
